note: A drill may be this much wider than the hole: 0.004 in exactly — 0.1 mm rounded it down and rejected a tool a thousandth of a millimetre inside the band; the engine itself uses 0.001 in (the API's largest drill diameter)
A drill may be this much narrower than the hole: 0.004 in exactly — a 0.075 in drill in a 0.079 in hole is in the band
column5: and 0.1 mm put it out of it

note: A drill tip may be this much shallower (wider) than a blind hole's bottom: engine drillAngleTolerancePlus
A drill tip may be this much sharper than the bottom; 0 because a sharper tip leaves a step: engine drillAngleToleranceMinus
The largest bull-nose radius that may stand in for a flat end on a floor the model draws sharp: engine maxBullnoseEndmillFinishingRadius 0.001 in
How far a through cut runs past the bottom: engine through_feature_overcut_finish 0.005 in (rough is 0.010 in)
How far a chamfer or dovetail tool's angle may differ from the feature's: engine chamfer_angle_tolerance_rad
A thread mill stays this much under the minor diameter: engine 0.98 × minor

Share of the overall length that stays in the holder: the stickout runs from the flute length up to what leaves this much — 2/3 of the tool out at most — and an assembly holding at least this much is good
Share of the overall length in the holder below which an assembly is not compatible: a quarter
Room wanted between the holder and the part sideways: 0.02 in; engine radial_holder_clearance 0.01 in
Room wanted between the holder nose and the part top: 0.02 in; engine axial_holder_clearance 0.01 in
The shortest stickout worth setting a tool up at: 0.5 in — the default stands out at least this far where the tool's length allows
The default stickout lands on this increment for inch tools: 1/8 in — the step nearest what the holder needs and never under it
The default stickout lands on this increment for metric tools

How much of the shank stays in the holder where the manufacturer does not say, in diameters — ISO 13399 calls it LSCN, clamping length minimum, against the shank diameter DMM. 3×D is the rule of thumb; the manufacturers publish 4 to 6 (Seco 410050R050 wants 36 mm of a ⌀6 shank). A tool that states its own is read from that instead.
